hook.text: The Emancipation Proclamation freed slaves in 1863. Enslaved people in Texas didn't learn until 1865.

buildup.text: On June 19, 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, and announced the war—and slavery—were over.

discovery.text: Freed communities began celebrating the date immediately. It became the oldest African American holiday.

twist.text: Juneteenth wasn't a federal holiday until 2021—156 years after the event. Recognition came late.

climax.text: The gap between law and reality is the real lesson. Freedom on paper isn't freedom in life.

punchline.text: Liberation delayed is liberation's own story.

quiz.question: When did Juneteenth become a US federal holiday?
